mcqs.question: A force of 10 N is applied perpendicular to a lever arm that is 0.2 m long about a fixed pivot. What is the magnitude of the torque (moment of force) produced?
mcqs.explanation: Torque is calculated as τ = F × r, where F is the magnitude of the force and r is the perpendicular distance (lever arm) from the axis. Here τ = 10 N × 0.2 m = 2 N·m. A common mistake is to forget the distance or to treat the force as already a torque, leading to the incorrect 10 N·m answer.

mcqs.question: For a given force magnitude, at which position relative to the axis of rotation is the lever arm the greatest?

options.A: When the line of action of the force passes through the axis
options.B: When the point of application is farthest from the axis
options.C: When the force makes an angle of 45° with the lever
options.D: The lever arm is the same at all positions

mcqs.answer: When the point of application is farthest from the axis
mcqs.explanation: The lever arm is the perpendicular distance from the axis to the line of action of the force. Increasing this distance increases the lever arm. Therefore, the farthest point from the axis gives the maximum lever arm. Options A and D are incorrect because they give zero or constant lever arm, and option C does not guarantee the maximum perpendicular distance.

mcqs.question: A rectangular door is hinged on its left side. Force A pushes upward on the right edge of the door, while Force B pushes downward on the same edge. Which statement correctly compares the directions of the torques produced by the two forces?

options.C: Force A produces a clockwise torque, while Force B produces an anticlockwise torque.
options.D: Force A produces an anticlockwise torque, while Force B produces a clockwise torque.

mcqs.answer: Force A produces an anticlockwise torque, while Force B produces a clockwise torque.
mcqs.explanation: Torque direction follows the right‑hand rule or the sense of rotation. An upward force on the right side tends to rotate the door anticlockwise about the left hinge, whereas a downward force on the same side tends to rotate it clockwise. Hence option D is correct; the other options incorrectly assign the same sense to both forces.

mcqs.question: A uniform rod 2 m long and weighing 40 N is hinged at its left end. A force F is applied upward at a point 0.5 m from the hinge. To keep the rod in rotational equilibrium about the hinge, what must be the magnitude of F?
mcqs.explanation: For equilibrium, the total clockwise torque must equal the total anticlockwise torque. The weight acts at the centre (1 m from the hinge) producing a clockwise torque of 40 N × 1 m = 40 N·m. The upward force F at 0.5 m produces an anticlockwise torque of F × 0.5 m. Setting them equal: F × 0.5 = 40 ⇒ F = 80 N. Options A, B, and D give incorrect torque balances.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines torque?

options.A: The product of mass and acceleration of a body.
options.B: The turning effect of a force about a specified axis or point.
options.C: The rate of change of linear momentum.
options.D: The force exerted per unit area.

mcqs.answer: The turning effect of a force about a specified axis or point.
mcqs.explanation: Torque (or moment of force) quantifies how effectively a force can cause rotational motion about an axis. Option B captures this definition. Option A describes force (Newton's second law), C describes impulse, and D describes pressure.

mcqs.question: A force of 15 N acts at an angle of 90° to a lever arm that is 0.4 m long. What is the moment of force about the pivot?
mcqs.explanation: When the force is perpendicular to the lever arm, torque τ = F × r. Here τ = 15 N × 0.4 m = 6 N·m. Option B mistakenly treats the force as torque, C uses an incorrect multiplication, and D would be true only if the force line passed through the pivot.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the lever arm from the line of action of a force?

options.A: The lever arm is the direction of the force; the line of action is the distance from the axis.
options.B: The lever arm is the perpendicular distance from the axis to the line of action; the line of action is the straight line along which the force acts.
options.C: Both terms refer to the same concept and can be used interchangeably.
options.D: The lever arm is always equal to the magnitude of the force.

mcqs.answer: The lever arm is the perpendicular distance from the axis to the line of action; the line of action is the straight line along which the force acts.
mcqs.explanation: The lever arm (or moment arm) is a distance, measured perpendicularly from the axis to the line of action of the force. The line of action is the infinite line extending in the direction of the force. Option B states this correctly. Options A, C, and D confuse the definitions.

mcqs.question: A wrench of length 0.3 m is used to tighten a bolt. The applied force is directed downward at the end of the wrench. What is the direction of the torque produced about the bolt (axis) when viewed from above?

options.C: No torque because the force is vertical

mcqs.explanation: When the force is applied downward at the end of the wrench, it tends to rotate the bolt in a clockwise sense as seen from above. The torque direction follows the right‑hand rule: curl fingers from the lever arm toward the force direction; the thumb points into the page, indicating clockwise rotation. Option B is opposite, C ignores the perpendicular component, and D is physically impossible.
